newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO says yen should be at 100/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO says yen should be at 100/dlr.

text.p: Chrysler Corp chief executive Robert Eaton said on Thursday he believed the dollar was overvalued against the yen and should be trading at a rate of about 100 yen to the dollar.
Speaking to reporters at a reception, Eaton said the current exchange rate of about 109 yen to the dollar was giving a price advantage to Japanese auto makers.
"I think that right now the structural rate is about 100 (yen to the dollar). And I think it will go down from there as their inflation" falls below that of the United States, he said.

If the yen drops to the 100 level or below, it would increase the cost of goods imported from Japan, including automobiles and automotive parts. For the 1997 model year, several Japanese car makers have introduced new vehicles priced equal to or below the models they replace.
On Monday, Ford Motor Co chairman and chief executive Alex Trotman said he thought the current rate of exchange was threatening U.S. competitiveness in the automobile and other industries.

Eaton said he had not expressed his views about the exchange rate with government officials since news of a widening trade deficit was released on Wednesday. In the past he has urged the Clinton administration to keep the dollar from strengthening against the yen.
